item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q020_syntaxin_fragment_reclassification","answer":"SCOPe’s current treatment means that 1br0 and 1ez3 should be interpreted as incomplete realizations of the syntaxin N-terminal domain represented more fully by 1dn1 chain B, not as independent evidence for distinct folds. Any topology inferred from 1br0 or 1ez3 applies only to the retained fragment; omitted helices and long-range contacts can change the apparent fold. Thus 1dn1B is the safer representative for whole-domain comparisons and template selection, while the fragments are suitable only for modeling their covered regions. Their placement with the complete syntaxin domain can support family-level common ancestry when combined with sequence identity and matching construct boundaries, but local fragment similarity alone cannot establish homology to unrelated proteins, justify transfer of full-domain interactions or syntaxin function, or imply evolutionary fold switching. Biological conclusions should therefore be checked against full-domain structural alignment, sequence evidence, and PDB construct/residue boundaries rather than inherited from an old fragment-based fold label.","evidence_used":["pretrained model knowledge"]}]}
